original_idea.title: Diversity-Aware Ensemble Safety Evaluation Framework
original_idea.problem: Current AI safety evaluations treat model outputs independently. There is no framework for asking whether a portfolio of deployed models provides diverse enough coverage to catch failures that any single model misses.
original_idea.direction: Design a formal framework borrowing from portfolio theory: given N deployed models, define an 'effective diversity coverage' metric for safety tasks, and show empirically that homogeneous portfolios have lower coverage than heterogeneous ones.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Regulators and deployers need tools to reason about system-level safety, not just individual-model safety.
original_idea.relevant_context: Financial systemic risk literature on concentration risk and correlated defaults (CEPR 2024) provides ready-made mathematical machinery. RLHF has been shown to reduce diversity compared to SFT (ICLR 2024).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: a theoretical framework for portfolio diversity is useful for regulators, but the chain from framework design to improved safety outcomes has an intermediate gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: requires portfolio theory mathematics and formal framework design, which is challenging for beginner CS students without quantitative finance background.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: defining metrics formally, implementing them, and providing empirical validation across multiple model portfolios is substantial work.

novelty.reasoning: No published work formalizes a portfolio-theory-based 'effective diversity coverage' metric for AI safety model portfolios. Financial systemic risk literature on concentration risk exists independently. IOSCO's 2025 AI Working Group identified concentration risk in financial AI deployments. The Artificial Hivemind documents homogeneity but does not propose portfolio-level diversity metrics. The cross-disciplinary application of portfolio theory to AI safety evaluation is mostly novel, though the complexity makes it challenging for the target audience.
